questions.question:
Which of the following statements are correct regarding the National Annual Report and Index on Women's Safety (NARI) 2025?
1. Kohima ranked the highest in the NARI 2025 index.
2. Mumbai scored 68.7% for public transport security and civic participation.
3. Delhi ranked poorly at 56.2% due to infrastructure gaps.
4. Patna, Jaipur, and Faridabad ranked highly for their women-friendly policies and infrastructure in the NARI 2025 report.
questions.solution:
Solution

The correct answer is Option 1, 2 and 3.

In News
The National Commission for Women (NCW) has released the National Annual Report and Index on Women's Safety (NARI) 2025, India's first comprehensive perception-based assessment of women's safety in urban centers.

Key Points
The NARI 2025 survey, covering 12,770 women across 31 cities, reveals that 40% of urban women feel unsafe, highlighting the gap between official crime statistics and women's lived experiences.
The methodology integrates official crime data with perceptions and lived experiences, revealing a "dark figure" of unreported harassment.
Top Performing Cities:
Kohima (82.9%) tops the index, recognized for its gender equity practices, community policing, and inclusive governance.
Visakhapatnam (78.2%) and Bhubaneswar (75.8%) are also ranked highly for infrastructure, policing, and women-friendly policies.
Northeastern cities like Aizawl, Gangtok, and Itanagar performed well due to community solidarity and inclusive governance.
Challenges in Metropolitan Areas:
Mumbai stands out with a 68.7% score for robust public transport security and civic participation.
Delhi (56.2%) and Kolkata (54.8%) rank poorly due to infrastructure gaps, high crime perceptions, and patriarchal norms.
Bottom Performers:
Ranchi (52.3%) and Srinagar (53.1%) are the lowest ranked, reflecting weak institutional responsiveness and security concerns.
Patna, Jaipur, and Faridabad show how inadequate urban planning and patriarchal norms contribute to insecurity.
Hence,
Statement 4 is INCORRECT.

Additional Information
Harassment Patterns:
7% of urban women experienced harassment in public spaces, rising to 14% among women under 24.
The majority of incidents were verbal harassment (58%), followed by physical (39%) and psychological (10%) harassment.

questions.question: In which of the following years did Lala Lajpat Rai co-found Punjab National Bank?
questions.solution:
Solution
The correct answer is 1894.

Key Points
Lala Lajpat Rai, popularly known as Punjab Kesari, played a pivotal role in the establishment of the Punjab National Bank (PNB), which was registered on May 19, 1894, under the Indian Companies Act.
The bank was founded with the spirit of Swadeshi, aiming to create a truly Indian bank managed by Indians with Indian capital, serving as a landmark in the Indian banking history during the British Raj.
The first branch of Punjab National Bank opened for business on April 12, 1895, in Lahore (now in Pakistan), just a day before the Baisakhi festival.
Lala Lajpat Rai was the first person to open an account with the bank, and he was actively involved in its Board of Management during its foundational years.
The initiative was also supported by other prominent figures like Dyal Singh Majithia, who served as the first Chairman, and Lala Harkishen Lal.

Additional Information
Lala Lajpat Rai:
He was a key member of the Lal-Bal-Pal triumvirate along with Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Bipin Chandra Pal.
He founded the Servants of the People Society in 1921 and was elected President of the Indian National Congress in the Calcutta Special Session of 1920.
He famously led a protest against the Simon Commission in 1928, during which he suffered severe injuries from a lathi charge that eventually led to his death.
Punjab National Bank (PNB):
Following the Partition of India in 1947, the bank moved its headquarters from Lahore to New Delhi.
It was nationalized by the Government of India in July 1969 along with 13 other major commercial banks.
As of recent years, it remains one of the largest Public Sector Banks in India, having merged with the United Bank of India and Oriental Bank of Commerce in 2020.

During the 2025-26 fiscal year, a record capacity of 55.29 GW of non-fossil fuel-based electricity was installed.

Additional Information
Solar energy has seen massive growth, rising from 2.8 GW in 2014 to approximately 165 GW in 2026.
Wind energy capacity reached over 58 GW, up from 21 GW in 2014.
Renewable energy generation in India increased from 190.96 billion units in 2014-15 to 477.79 BU in 2025-26.
The capacity under the Approved List of Models and Manufacturers (ALMM) for Solar PV Modules crossed the historic 200 GW milestone.

The Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme has been instrumental in boosting domestic manufacturing and supply chain independence in the solar sector.

questions.testName: SSC CGL 2026: Officer’s Friday - Mega Live Test
questions.question:
Consider the following two statements, labeled Assertion (A) and Reason
(R). Evaluate them and choose the appropriate answer from the given options.

Assertion (A): The standard distance between the penalty spot and the goal line on a football field is 11 meters.
Reason
(R): This distance allows the goalkeeper a fair reaction time while challenging the accuracy and confidence of the penalty taker.

options.a: A is false, but R is true.
options.b: A is true, but R is false.
options.c: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.d: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A

questions.solution:
Solution

The correct answer is Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.

Key Points
The penalty spot in football is positioned 11 meters (12 yards) from the goal line as per the Laws of the Game set by FIFA.
This distance was formalized in 1891 when the penalty kick rule was introduced to ensure fairness and maintain a balance between the penalty taker and the goalkeeper.
The reasoning behind the distance is to provide the goalkeeper with a fair reaction time while simultaneously challenging the accuracy and confidence of the penalty taker.
The penalty kick is a direct free kick, and only the penalty taker and the goalkeeper are allowed to be in the penalty area during the kick.
The goalkeeper must remain on the goal line until the penalty is taken but may move laterally to prepare for the shot.

Additional Information
Penalty Kick Overview:
Introduced in 1891 as a measure to prevent intentional fouls near the goal.
A penalty kick is awarded when a player commits a direct free kick offense inside their own penalty area.
The penalty spot is a fixed point from which the penalty taker must shoot the ball.
FIFA Laws of the Game:
The Laws of the Game are maintained by the International Football Association Board (IFAB), with FIFA as a key member.
These laws dictate the dimensions and markings on the football field, including the penalty area and spot.
Goalkeeper Rules During a Penalty:
The goalkeeper must have at least part of one foot touching, or in line with, the goal line until the ball is kicked.
Moving forward off the goal line before the penalty is taken results in a retake if a goal is not scored.
Psychological Aspects of Penalty Kicks:
Penalty kicks test the mental focus and composure of both the penalty taker and the goalkeeper.
Studies show that penalty shootouts are often influenced by psychological pressure and confidence.
Historical Context:
The penalty kick was first used in a competitive match in 1891 during an Irish Cup semi-final.
It has since become a crucial part of football, used to resolve matches tied after extra time in knockout tournaments.

questions.question: The first Indian Budget was presented by James Wilson, a Scottish economist. When was it presented?
questions.solution:
Solution
The correct answer is 1860.

Key Points
The first Indian Budget was formally introduced to the Legislative Council on 7th April 1860.
It was presented by James Wilson, a Scottish economist and politician who served as the Finance Member of the Viceroy’s Council of India.
The presentation of this budget followed the administrative transition of India from the East India Company to the British Crown under the Government of India Act 1858.
James Wilson proposed this budget to address the severe financial crisis and heavy debt incurred by the British administration following the Indian Rebellion of 1857.
One of the most significant features of this budget was the introduction of Income Tax in India, which was met with substantial opposition from the local population and merchants.
Wilson also founded The Economist magazine and the Standard Chartered Bank, bringing significant economic expertise to the British Raj.

Additional Information
Post-Independence Budgeting:
The first Budget of Independent India was presented on 26th November 1947 by the first Finance Minister, R.K. Shanmukham Chetty.
The first Republic Day Budget was presented by John Mathai in 1950.
Morarji Desai holds the record for presenting the maximum number of budgets (10) in Indian history.
The Railway Budget, which was separated from the Union Budget in 1924 based on the Acworth Committee recommendations, was merged back into the Union Budget in 2017.
Until 1999, the Union Budget was presented at 5 PM on the last working day of February, but Yashwant Sinha changed the timing to 11 AM.

questions.testName: SSC CGL 2026: Officer’s Friday - Mega Live Test
questions.question: Which of the following fossil parks has the second-largest hatchery of dinosaur eggs in the world?
questions.solution:
Solution
The correct answer is Indroda Dinosaur and Fossil Park.

Key Points
Indroda Dinosaur and Fossil Park, located in Gandhinagar, Gujarat, is widely regarded as the second-largest hatchery of dinosaur eggs in the world, surpassed only by a site in Aix-en-Provence, France.
The park is spread over an area of about 400 hectares on the banks of the Sabarmati River and is managed by the Gujarat Ecological Education and Research (GEER) Foundation.
It houses a massive collection of fossilized dinosaur eggs and skeletal remains, primarily belonging to the Late Cretaceous period (approximately 66 million years ago).
The fossils found here, including those of the Rajasaurus narmadensis, were excavated from the Songhir Bagh Basin and the Balasinor region of Gujarat.
The park features life-size fiberglass models of various dinosaurs such as Tyrannosaurus rex, Megalosaurus, and Titanosaurus to educate visitors about prehistoric life.

Additional Information
Mandla Plant Fossils National Park:
Located in Madhya Pradesh, this park preserves fossils of plants that existed in India between 40 million and 150 million years ago.
The fossils are found in a petrified state across seven villages in the Mandla district.
Siwalik Fossil Park:
Also known as Suketi Fossil Park, it is situated in the Sirmaur district of Himachal Pradesh.
It is famous for its Cenozoic mammalian fossils and contains life-size models of extinct animals like the Giant Elephant and Saber-toothed tiger.
National Fossil Wood Park:
Located in Tiruvakkarai, Tamil Nadu, it contains petrified wood fossils dating back to the Mio-Pliocene age (approximately 20 million years ago).
The park is maintained by the Geological Survey of India (GSI).

Solution

The correct answer is Henry Chandler Cowles.
Key Points
Henry Chandler Cowles studied ecological succession in the Indiana Dunes of Northwest Indiana in the 1890s.
Henry Chandler Cowles (1869-1939) was a University of Chicago botany professor and conservationist, his studies of plant life in the Indiana Dunes made Cowles one of America's most notable early ecologists.
In 1896, Cowles traveled to the southern shore of Lake Michigan to see the Indiana Dunes for the first time and studied them.
His study explained the development and distribution of local plant communities in terms of topography, moisture, wind, erosion, sedimentation, and other geological processes.

Additional Information
G Evelyn Hutchinson was a British ecologist sometimes described as the "father of modern ecology".
Frederic Clements was an American botanist, taxonomist, and ecologist who influenced the early study of plant communities, particularly the process of plant succession.
Charles Sutherland Elton FRS was an English zoologist and animal ecologist associated with the development of population and community ecology, including studies of invasive organisms.

questions.question: Who among the following has been appointed as the Comptroller General of India in November 2024?
questions.solution:
Solution

The correct answer is K Sanjay Murthy.

Key Points
K Sanjay Murthy was appointed as the Comptroller General of India in November 2024.
The Comptroller General of India is a crucial constitutional authority responsible for auditing the revenue and expenditure of the Government of India.
K Sanjay Murthy has previously served in key administrative roles, contributing significantly to public administration and governance.
This appointment was made to ensure the effective management and oversight of public funds, enhancing transparency and accountability.
The Comptroller General of India operates under the provisions of Article 148 of the Indian Constitution.

Additional Information
Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG):
The CAG is an independent authority established under Article 148 of the Constitution of India.

questions.question: The tribal festival of Bhagoria is traditionally celebrated a week prior to which Hindu festival?
questions.solution:
Solution

The correct answer is Holika Dahan.

Key Points
The tribal festival of Bhagoria is celebrated predominantly by the Bhil and Bhilala tribes of the Indian states of Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra.
It is traditionally celebrated a week prior to the Hindu festival of Holika Dahan, which marks the beginning of the spring season.
Bhagoria Haat: The festival is celebrated in the form of a fair known as the Bhagoria Haat, which acts as a marketplace and marriage fair where eligible young individuals choose their life partners.
The celebration involves vibrant cultural activities, including tribal dance, music, and rituals that reflect the rich tradition and customs of these communities.
The name "Bhagoria" is derived from the word 'Bhag' (to run away), symbolizing the tradition where couples elope and later gain acceptance from their families.
The festival coincides with agricultural activities, marking the completion of harvesting and symbolizing prosperity and joy.
Holika Dahan: This festival, also known as Chhoti Holi, is celebrated one day before Holi to signify the victory of good over evil, particularly the mythological story of Prahlada and Holika.
The association of Bhagoria with Holika Dahan highlights the tribal communities' integration of their customs with broader Hindu festivals. Hence, the correct answer is Holika Dahan.

Additional Information
Bhagoria Festival:
The Bhagoria festival is an integral part of the indigenous culture of the Bhil and Bhilala tribes, celebrated with enthusiasm and joy.
Location: It is primarily celebrated in the Jhabua and Alirajpur districts of Madhya Pradesh and in parts of Maharashtra.
The festival serves as an occasion for social bonding and allows tribal communities to showcase their unique traditions.
Holika Dahan:
Date: Holika Dahan occurs on the Purnima (full moon) night of the Hindu lunar month of Phalguna, generally in February or March.
It symbolises the victory of good over evil, commemorating the tale of Prahlada, a devotee of Lord Vishnu, and Holika, his evil aunt.
The festival is celebrated by lighting bonfires and performing rituals to cleanse negativity and bring prosperity.
Tribal Festivals:
Tribal festivals like Bhagoria reflect the distinct cultural heritage of indigenous communities in India.
They often coincide with agricultural cycles, emphasizing the importance of nature and community in tribal life.
Other notable tribal festivals include Hornbill Festival in Nagaland and Baneshwar Fair in Rajasthan.

Important Points

Distinctive Cultural Practices:
Bhagoria Haat is a rare festival that combines social, cultural, and economic aspects, serving as a marriage fair and a market for tribal communities.
The vibrant costumes, traditional music, and colorful rituals during Bhagoria showcase the rich tribal heritage of the region.
Connection with Holika Dahan:
The timing of Bhagoria, a week before Holika Dahan, integrates tribal festivities with the broader Hindu tradition, reflecting cultural syncretism.
Both festivals signify joy, renewal, and the celebration of life, highlighting the importance of community and tradition.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 2
questions.question: Which statement correctly states the legal effect of Article 255 regarding assent to bills?

options.a: A State law becomes invalid without a written assent from the Governor.
options.b: Assent must always be explicitly mentioned for the law to operate.
options.c: A law remains valid even if prior recommendation was missing, provided assent is given later.
options.d: Presidential assent must be obtained before the bill passes in the legislature.

questions.solution:
Solution

The correct answer is A law remains valid even if prior recommendation was missing, provided assent is given later..

Key Points
Article 255 of the Constitution of India deals with the validity of laws even in cases where the prior recommendation or assent required was not initially obtained.
It states that if the required recommendation is missing, the law will not become invalid, as long as the necessary assent is given later.
This provision ensures that procedural lapses in obtaining prior recommendation do not affect the legality or enforceability of the law. Hence, the
statement is correct.
For example, a bill requiring the Governor's recommendation or the President's assent can still be validated if the assent is granted subsequently, as per Article 255.
It ensures smooth legislative functioning and avoids unnecessary invalidation of laws due to procedural errors. Hence, the correct option explains this legal safeguard.

Additional Information
Article 255 of the Constitution of India:
Article 255 is aimed at ensuring that minor procedural lapses do not result in the invalidation of laws or legislative decisions.
It provides flexibility in cases where prior recommendations (Governor’s or President’s) may not have been obtained initially but are granted later.
Example: If a state legislature passes a bill requiring the President's prior recommendation, the bill remains valid if the President grants assent afterward.
Role of Assent in Legislative Process:
Assent is the final approval required for a bill to become law. It can be granted by the Governor or the President, depending on the type of bill.
Bills requiring prior recommendation include money bills and bills affecting the powers or interests of the states.
Examples of Legislative Safeguards:
The provision under Article 255 has been used to validate laws passed without prior recommendation, ensuring legislative efficiency.
For example, financial bills requiring the Governor’s recommendation can still be validated after the Governor grants assent.

Important Points

Legal Validity of Laws:
Article 255 ensures that procedural lapses in obtaining prior recommendation do not automatically invalidate a law. It is a significant safeguard to avoid legislative disruptions.
This provision highlights the importance of assent in validating laws and ensures the smooth functioning of legislative processes.
Key Characteristics of Article 255:
It applies to cases requiring prior recommendations such as financial bills or bills impacting federal relations.
It ensures flexibility in legislative procedures, allowing the assent to be granted later without affecting the law’s validity.

Jamini Roy

He rejected his own training received at the Government School of Art, Calcutta.
Being a student of Abanindranath Tagore, he realised the futility of pursuing academic art.
He noticed that the rural, folk art in Bengal had much in common with how modern European masters like Picasso and Paul Klee painted.
​After all, Picasso had arrived at Cubism by learning from the use of bold forms found in African masks.
Roy, too, used simple and pure colours.
Like village artists, he also made his own colours from vegetables and minerals. Hence,
statement 1 is correct.
His art lent itself to easy reproduction by other members in his family, quite like the artisanal practice followed in villages.
However, what differentiated his art from that of village artists was that Roy signed on his paintings.  Hence,
statement 2 is correct.
His style is seen as uniquely personal, distinct from both the academic naturalism of art schools and from Raja Ravi Varma’s Indianised naturalism, as well as, from the delicate style practised by some of the Bengal School artists.

The 343 km long, access-controlled six-lane Bengaluru-Kadapa-Vijayawada Economic Corridor has been designed for a safe, high-speed, and scenic travel experience. questions.question: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched regarding the animals and their respective phylum?
questions.solution:
Option c is correct: Whale is not a true fish - it is an aquatic mammal belonging to the phylum Chordata, class Mammalia (order Cetacea). Like all mammals, whales are warm-blooded, breathe through lungs (surfacing periodically for air), give birth to live young, and nurse them with milk - none of which are fish characteristics.

Why the other options are incorrect:
(a). Jellyfish - Mollusca (Incorrect): Jellyfish actually belong to the phylum Coelenterata (Cnidaria), not Mollusca. They have a simple radially symmetrical body with a central body cavity (coelenteron) and stinging cells (cnidocytes/nematocysts) - a hallmark feature of cnidarians. Mollusca instead includes soft-bodied animals like snails, octopuses, and clams.

(b). Crayfish - Insecta (Incorrect): Crayfish belong to the phylum Arthropoda, but within class Crustacea, not Insecta. Crustaceans (like crabs, prawns, and crayfish) typically have two pairs of antennae and gills for respiration, while insects have one pair of antennae, three pairs of legs, and (usually) wings - key distinguishing features.

(d). Devil fish - Coelenterate (Incorrect): "Devil fish" commonly refers to the manta ray (or sometimes an octopus, depending on regional usage), which - if referring to the manta ray - belongs to phylum Chordata, class Chondrichthyes (cartilaginous fish), not Coelenterata.

questions.question: What is the primary step that occurs during aerobic respiration in plants?
questions.solution:
Solution

CONCEPT:

Aerobic Respiration

Aerobic respiration is the process by which cells produce energy in the form of ATP by breaking down glucose in the presence of oxygen.
It involves multiple steps: glycolysis, the Krebs cycle, and the electron transport chain.
The primary and initial step of aerobic respiration is glycolysis.
Glycolysis occurs in the cytoplasm and does not require oxygen directly. It breaks down one molecule of glucose into two molecules of pyruvate, producing ATP and NADH in the process.

EXPLANATION:

In plants, during aerobic respiration:
Glycolysis is the first step that occurs in the cytoplasm.
In this step, glucose is broken down into two molecules of pyruvate.
Pyruvate then enters the mitochondria for further steps, which include the Krebs cycle and the electron transport chain.

Additional Information
Fermentation (Option 2) is an anaerobic process and does not occur in the presence of oxygen.
Anaerobic respiration (Option 3) is respiration in the absence of oxygen and is not part of aerobic respiration.
Pyrolysis (Option 4) is a thermal decomposition process and is unrelated to cellular respiration.

Therefore, the correct answer is Glycolysis.

Subroto Mukherjee is widely regarded as the Father of the Indian Air Force. He played a pivotal role in shaping the Indian Air Force (IAF) into a modern and independent entity. Hence, Assertion (A) is correct.
He was the first Indian Chief of Air Staff, assuming office on 1 April 1954. During his tenure, he led the transition of the Indian Air Force from a colonial force to an independent and modernized organization. Hence, Reason

The reason

Additional Information
Subroto Mukherjee's Contributions:
Born on 5 March 1911, Subroto Mukherjee was one of the first batch of Indians to be trained at the Royal Air Force College in Cranwell, United Kingdom.
He joined the Indian Air Force in 1932, which at the time was a part of the British Royal Air Force.
His vision and leadership helped the IAF evolve from a support service to a strategic force capable of independent operations.
Role as Air Chief Marshal:

Under his leadership, the IAF expanded its operational capabilities and introduced modern aircraft into its fleet.
He emphasized training and professional development, ensuring the IAF was equipped to meet national defense challenges.
Indian Air Force Evolution:
The IAF was established on 8 October 1932 as an auxiliary force of the Royal Air Force.
During World War II, the IAF played a crucial role in supporting British operations in Southeast Asia.
Post-independence, the IAF became an integral part of India's defense system, with leaders like Subroto Mukherjee driving its growth.
Legacy:
Subroto Mukherjee's contributions are celebrated annually on Air Force Day, observed on 8 October.
He passed away in 1960, but his legacy continues to inspire generations of air force personnel.

questions.question: 'Shad Suk Mynsiem' festival is celebrated in which of the following states?
questions.solution:
Solution

The correct answer is Meghalaya.

Key Points
Shad Suk Mynsiem, meaning "Dance of Contentment," is a prominent festival celebrated by the Khasi tribe of Meghalaya.
It is an annual spring festival observed to honor the harvest season and express gratitude to the divine creator U Blei for blessings and prosperity.
The festival is marked by traditional dance performances where both men and women participate. Men symbolize protectors, while women symbolize fertility and prosperity.
It is celebrated according to Khasi customs and traditions, and the event is organized by the Seng Khasi, a socio-religious organization dedicated to preserving Khasi culture.
The festival typically occurs in April, attracting locals and tourists alike to witness the vibrant cultural display and rituals.

Additional Information
Meghalaya:
Meghalaya, meaning "Abode of Clouds," is a state in northeastern India, formed in 1972.
The state is known for its rich biodiversity, scenic landscapes, and unique culture.
Meghalaya is inhabited by three main tribal groups: Khasi, Garo, and Jaintia.
The state is famous for its living root bridges, Mawsmai caves, and Cherrapunji, one of the wettest places on Earth.
Other Festivals of Meghalaya:
Wangala Festival: Celebrated by the Garo tribe to mark the harvest season and honor their deity Saljong.
Behdienkhlam Festival: Celebrated by the Jaintia tribe to drive away evil spirits and invoke blessings for a good harvest.
Nongkrem Dance: A traditional Khasi festival celebrated to seek blessings for a bountiful harvest.
Khasi Tribe:
The Khasi people follow a matrilineal system, where lineage and inheritance pass through the female line.
Their religion, Niam Khasi, is based on reverence for nature and ancestral spirits.
The Khasi language is a part of the Mon-Khmer family of languages.
Importance of Festivals:
Festivals like Shad Suk Mynsiem play a vital role in preserving the cultural heritage and traditions of indigenous communities.
They foster a sense of identity and pride among tribal groups and promote tourism in the region.
These celebrations also serve as a medium to convey social values, such as gratitude, community participation, and harmony with nature.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mentions that ‘All the executive action of the Government of a state shall be expressed to be taken in the name of the Governor’?
questions.solution:
Solution
The correct answer is Article 166(1)

Key Points
Article 166(1) of the Indian Constitution states that all executive actions of the Government of a State shall be expressed to be taken in the name of the Governor.
This provision ensures that the Governor, as the nominal head of the state, is the authority in whose name the executive actions are carried out.
The article is part of Chapter II of the Constitution, which deals with the Executive power of the State.
It establishes a formal procedure for the conduct of government business and maintains the constitutional framework of the state executive.
Article 166(1) - States that all executive actions of a State Government shall be expressed in the name of the Governor.
Article 163(1) - Specifies that there shall be a Council of Ministers with the Chief Minister at the head to aid and advise the Governor in the exercise of his functions, except where the Governor is required to act at his discretion.
Article 164(1) - Deals with the appointment of the Chief Minister and other ministers by the Governor and states that the ministers shall hold office during the pleasure of the Governor.
Article 165(1) - Provides for the appointment of the Advocate-General for the State by the Governor and mentions that he shall hold office during the pleasure of the Governor.

Additional Information
The Constitution of India was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 26th November 1949 and came into effect on 26th January 1950.
It lays down the framework defining fundamental political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
The Constitution of India is the longest written constitution of any country in the world.
It declares India a sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.
The Seventh Schedule of the Constitution contains three lists which delineate the subjects under the Union, State, and Concurrent lists.
Amendments to the Constitution can be made through a process outlined in Article 368.
The Union List has been amended several times to meet the evolving needs of the nation.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. Nati dance is performed in Himachal Pradesh exclusively during the Dussehra festival in Shimla.
2. Kinnauri dance is a traditional group dance of the tribal communities of Himachal Pradesh.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
Solution

The correct answer is Option 2 (Only 2).

Key Points
Statement 1: The statement claims that Nati dance is performed in Himachal Pradesh exclusively during the Dussehra festival in Shimla. This is incorrect.
The Nati dance is a traditional folk dance of Himachal Pradesh and is performed in various festivals and celebrations across the state, not exclusively during the Dussehra festival in Shimla.
It is performed in different parts of Himachal Pradesh, including Kullu, Shimla, and Sirmaur, and is recognized as one of the world's largest folk dance performances in terms of participation.
Statement 2: The statement mentions that Kinnauri dance is a traditional group dance of the tribal communities of Himachal Pradesh. This is correct.
The Kinnauri dance is an integral part of the cultural heritage of Kinnaur, a tribal district in Himachal Pradesh.
It is performed in traditional attire by both men and women, often during religious ceremonies, festivals, and social gatherings.
The dance is characterized by synchronized movements, simple rhythmic steps, and is accompanied by traditional musical instruments like drums and horns.
Hence, only
Statement 2 is correct, making Option 2 the correct answer.

Additional Information
About Nati Dance:
The Nati dance is a popular folk dance of Himachal Pradesh, particularly in the Kullu valley.
It has been recognized in the Guinness Book of World Records as the largest folk dance performance in terms of participation, with over 9,800 women performing it together in Kullu.
It is performed during various festivals like Dussehra, weddings, and other celebrations, typically accompanied by traditional instruments like 'dhol' and 'nagara'.
About Kinnauri Dance:
The Kinnauri dance is a traditional group dance performed by the tribal communities of the Kinnaur district in Himachal Pradesh.
It is deeply rooted in the religious and cultural practices of the Kinnauri people and is often performed during festivals like Phulaich (flower festival).
The performers wear vibrant and traditional attire, including woolen garments and jewelry, while dancing in synchronized movements.
Other Folk Dances of Himachal Pradesh:
Chham: A masked dance performed by Lamas in monasteries, symbolizing the victory of good over evil.
Thoda: A martial dance form performed during traditional archery events.
Gugga Dance: Performed to honor the folk deity Gugga Ji.
Importance of Dance in Himachal Culture:
Folk dances like Nati and Kinnauri represent the cultural and social values of the region.
They showcase the lifestyle, traditions, and beliefs of the local communities and serve as a medium of storytelling.
Dance performances are also an important aspect of tourism, attracting visitors to experience the rich cultural heritage of the state.

Important Points

Himachal Pradesh's Cultural Diversity: The state is home to a variety of tribes and communities, each with its own unique traditions, dances, and festivals.
UNESCO Recognition: The Kullu Dussehra festival, though not exclusive to Nati dance, has been listed as an Intangible Cultural Heritage by UNESCO.
Tourism and Economy: Himachal's folk dances play a significant role in promoting cultural tourism, contributing to the state's economy.
Preservation Efforts: Various organizations and festivals are working towards preserving and promoting traditional dance forms of Himachal Pradesh.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 6
questions.question: Water reabsorption from the distal part of the renal tubule is under the control of which hormone?
questions.solution:
Solution

CONCEPT:

Water Reabsorption in the Distal Renal Tubule

Water reabsorption in the kidneys, specifically in the distal part of the renal tubule and collecting duct, is regulated by hormones to maintain fluid balance and blood pressure.
The hormone primarily responsible for controlling water reabsorption in this region is Vasopressin, also known as antidiuretic hormone (ADH).
Vasopressin is secreted by the posterior pituitary gland and acts on the kidneys to increase the permeability of the distal tubule and collecting ducts to water.

EXPLANATION

Vasopressin binds to specific receptors on the cells of the distal tubule and collecting ducts.
This triggers the insertion of water channels called aquaporins into the cell membranes, allowing water to be reabsorbed back into the bloodstream.
This process helps conserve water in the body and concentrates the urine, especially during dehydration or low blood volume conditions.

Additional Information
Renin (Option 1): Involved in the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system, which regulates blood pressure and sodium balance.
Oxytocin (Option 3): A hormone involved in uterine contractions and milk ejection, not water reabsorption.
Angiotensin (Option 4): A component of the renin-angiotensin system, which indirectly influences water and salt retention but does not directly control water reabsorption in the distal tubule.
Therefore, the correct answer is Vasopressin.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Vairamudi Garudotsava:
1. It is primarily associated with the Mallikarjuna Swamy Temple in Tamilnadu.
2. It is a 10 to 13-day annual festival held in the Hindu month of Phalguna (March-April).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
Solution

The Correct Answer is Only 2.

Key Points
Vairamudi Garudotsava is primarily associated with the Cheluvanarayana Swamy Temple in Melukote, Mandya district, Karnataka.
It is a 10 to 13-day annual festival held in the Hindu month of Phalguna (March-April).
The Deity: Dedicated to Lord Cheluvanarayana Swamy (a form of Vishnu), also known as Thirunarayana or Ramapriya.
The Highlight (Vairamudi): The deity is adorned with a legendary diamond-studded crown called the Vairamudi (Vajramukuta).
Security: The crown is so valuable that it is kept in the Mandya District Treasury and brought to the temple under heavy armed escort only for this festival.
Ritual Secrecy: Tradition dictates that the crown must not be exposed to daylight; the head priest must fit it onto the deity while blindfolded or in the dark late at night.
It is believed that Garuda (Vishnu's celestial vehicle) brought the crown from the milky ocean after retrieving it from the demon Virochana.
Temple Style: The Cheluvanarayana Swamy Temple is primarily built in the Dravidian style, with significant influences from the Hoysala and Vijayanagara dynasties.
Key Patron: The 12th-century Srivaishnava saint Ramanujacharya stayed in Melukote for 12 years and was instrumental in renovating the temple and recovering the processional idol.
The temple is situated on the Yadavgiri (Yadugiri) hills. It features a large stepped stone pond called Kalyani Theertha.
The temple complex includes unique "sister ponds" known as Akka-Tangi Kola.

Additional Information
Karnataka hosts a diverse array of religious fairs (melas or jatras):

Mysuru Dasara (Nada Habba): While a state festival, its roots are deeply religious, celebrating the victory of Goddess Chamundeshwari over the demon Mahishasura. The 10-day event in September/October is famous for its royal festivities and the grand procession (Jumbo Savari) from the Mysuru Palace to Bannimantap.
Paryaya Festival (Udupi): A unique biennial festival held at the Udupi Krishna Temple. It involves the ceremonial transfer of administration of the temple among eight monasteries (Ashta Mathas), highlighting the region's distinct Vaishnavite traditions established by Saint Madhvacharya.
Kumbh Mela (T. Narasipura): Karnataka holds its own version of the Kumbh Mela every three years at T. Narasipura (Mysuru district), at the confluence of the Kaveri, Kabini, and mythical Spatika Sarovara rivers (Triveni Sangama). It is considered "Dakshina Kashi" and attracts lakhs of devotees for a holy dip.
Mahamastakabhisheka (Shravanabelagola): A key Jain pilgrimage event, this spectacular anointing ceremony for the 57-foot-tall monolithic statue of Lord Bahubali (Gomateshwara) is held once every 12 years. It is a major event for the Jain community.

With reference to the Baul tradition of Bengal, consider the following statements:

1) It is a mystical philosophy and music genre that emphasizes the search for the "Maner Manush" (the inner soul) while transcending formal religious boundaries.

2) The musical performances are traditionally characterized by the use of instruments such as the Ektara and the Dubki.

questions.solution:
The Baul tradition of Bengal is not just a musical style but a spiritual-philosophical movement. Bauls seek the "Maner Manush" or "the man of the heart," symbolizing the inner divine or the true self.

They reject rigid religious identities - Hindu, Muslim, or otherwise - and promote a humanistic, experiential spiritual path rooted in love, simplicity, and inner exploration.

Baul music is known for its simple yet soulful instruments. Two of the primary traditional instruments used are:

Ektara - A single-string plucked instrument, symbolic of the unity of God.

Dubki - A small percussion instrument (similar to a hand drum) used to maintain rhythm.

Further Insights
The Baul tradition is recognized by UNESCO as an Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity (2008).

Baul songs often emphasize love, humanity, and internal spiritual realization.

Bauls traditionally roam from village to village singing for food or alms.

Their music blends elements of Vaishnavism, Sufism, and Tantric traditions.

questions.question:
Given below are two statements, one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason
(R):

Assertion (A): The Governor of a State can allow the Union Government (or its officers) to carry out certain State-level executive functions, but only with the consent of the Government of India.

Reason
(R): Article 258A was added by the 7th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1956, to let States formally hand over certain administrative functions to the Centre.

In the context of the above statements, which of the following is correct?

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.c: A is true but R is false
options.d: A is false but R is true

questions.solution:
Assertion (A) - True

A Governor can allow the Central Government to perform certain State-level executive tasks, but only if the Government of India agrees.

This is directly allowed under Article 258A of the Constitution.

Reason
(R) - True

Article 258A was indeed added by the 7th Constitutional Amendment, 1956.

Its purpose was to create a two-way system in which:

the Centre can give its functions to States (Article 258), and

States can give their functions to the Centre (Article 258A).

Why R correctly explains A

The Assertion says the Governor can give some State functions to the Centre with the Centre's consent.

The Reason explains the exact constitutional article and the amendment that created this power.

So, R perfectly explains why A is true.

Further Insights
Article 258 allows the Centre to delegate tasks to States without amending the Constitution.

Administrative cooperation between Centre and States is a key feature of India's quasi-federal system.

With reference to the fundamental elements of a Raga in Indian Classical Music, consider the following statements:

1) Avroh refers to the ascending sequence of notes, while Aaroh represents the descending sequence of notes in a Raga.

2) The Vadi is the primary, most frequently used note (the "King"), whereas the Samvadi is the secondary important note (the "Minister").

questions.solution:
Vadi = Most important note

The Vadi is the dominant, most emphasized note of the raga.

It is often compared to a King because it is the central note around which the raga's character revolves.

Samvadi = Second-most important note

The Samvadi supports the Vadi like a "Minister," giving balance and stability to the raga.

Aaroh = Ascending
Avroh = Descending
Aaroh (Arohana): Notes go upwards
Avroh (Avarohana): Notes go downwards

Further Insights
A raga is built from selected notes (swaras) following specific rules.

The time of performance (prahar) can significantly affect a raga's emotional effect.

Some ragas use all seven notes (sampoorna), while others use five or six.

The Pakad is the signature phrase that helps identify a raga instantly.

Ragas evoke specific moods - called rasa, such as devotion, romance, or peace.

The Losar festival, celebrated in Ladakh, marks the beginning of the Tibetan New Year and is traditionally observed for ______ days.
questions.solution:
Losar (derived from 'Lo' meaning year and 'Sar' meaning new) is the most significant socio-religious festival of the Buddhist community in Ladakh. Although the most intense celebrations occur during the first three days, the festival is traditionally observed for a period of 15 days.

Further Insights:
Historical Context in Ladakh: Interestingly, Losar in Ladakh is often celebrated two months ahead of the standard Tibetan New Year. Legend traces this back to the 17th-century King Jamyang Namgyal, who decided to celebrate the New Year early before leading a military campaign in the winter.

Key Rituals:

Metho Ceremony: A procession where people carry flaming torches to drive away evil spirits and bad luck from the previous year.
Guthuk: A special noodle soup consumed on the eve of Losar, containing nine different ingredients.
Religious Offerings: Elaborate offerings called 'Tarzok' are made in monasteries and family shrines to ensure prosperity.
Significance: It symbolizes the victory of good over evil and is a time for family reunions, cleaning houses to welcome the new year, and performing traditional folk dances and songs.

questions.question: Who wrote the influential book "India: A Million Mutinies Now"?
questions.solution:
V.S. Naipaul wrote India: A Million Mutinies Now in 1990.

It is the final part of his famous "India" trilogy. Unlike his earlier, more critical books on India, this work is often seen as a more optimistic and empathetic narrative, where he travels across the country interviewing people from various walks of life to understand the growing complexities of post-independence India.

Further Insights:
The Trilogy: India: A Million Mutinies Now concludes a series that began with An Area of Darkness (1964) and continued with India: A Wounded Civilization (1977).
Theme: The "Million Mutinies" in the title refers to the countless small-scale social, political, and religious awakenings and assertions of identity across India that Naipaul witnessed during his travels. He viewed these not as a sign of collapse, but as a sign of a society's growth and democratization.
Awards: V.S. Naipaul, a Trinidadian-British writer of Indian descent, was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature in 2001.
Literary Style: The book is a masterpiece of travel writing and oral history, relying heavily on the voices of ordinary Indians - from Dalit activists to stockbrokers and religious leaders - to paint a panoramic picture of the nation.

questions.question: In the PMFBY (Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana), what is the fixed premium rate to be paid by farmers for all Kharif crops?
questions.solution:
The fixed premium rate to be paid by farmers for all Kharif crops under the PMFBY is 2.0%.

Under the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY), the premium rates are capped at a very low level to reduce the financial burden on farmers.

For all Kharif crops (summer/monsoon crops), the premium to be paid by the farmer is fixed at 2.0% of the sum insured or the actuarial rate, whichever is less.

Further Insights:
Government Subsidy: The difference between the actuarial premium rate (the actual market cost of the insurance) and the rate paid by the farmers is shared equally by the Central and State Governments as a subsidy.
Objective: Launched in 2016, PMFBY aims to provide a comprehensive insurance cover against the failure of the crop, thus helping in stabilizing the income of the farmers and encouraging them to adopt innovative practices.
Coverage: The scheme covers all stages of the crop cycle, including pre-sowing to post-harvest losses due to non-preventable natural risks such as drought, floods, landslides, pests, and diseases.

Revamped PMFBY (2.0): In 2020, the scheme was made voluntary for all farmers (earlier it was mandatory for loanee farmers). It also increased the flexibility for states to customize the scheme according to their local climatic risks.

questions.testName: SSC CGL 2026 [Sectional Timing] - Tier I- 3
questions.question: What is the maximum duration of a "Golden Score" (overtime) period in a standard Judo contest?

options.d: No time limit (until a score/penalty occurs)

questions.solution:
In a standard Judo contest, the Golden Score period has no time limit.

While some age-specific or local variations might impose a time limit for safety or scheduling, the official International Judo Federation (IJF) rules for senior competitions do not set a maximum duration for overtime.

In the past, Judo used a system called Hantei (judge's decision by flags), but this was replaced by the infinite Golden Score to ensure a winner is determined by technical action.

If a match ends in a draw after the regulation four minutes, it immediately enters the Golden Score phase. The clock is reset, and the contest continues indefinitely until one judoka achieves a score (Waza-ari or Ippon) or until one judoka receives a third penalty (Shido), resulting in disqualification (Hansoku-make).

Further Insights:
Carry-over: All scores and penalties (Shidos) accumulated during the regular four-minute match carry over into the Golden Score period.
Physical Endurance: Because there is no time limit, some high-level matches have been known to last over 10 to 15 minutes, making it an extreme test of physical and mental endurance.
Winning Criteria: The very first point awarded ends the match instantly. However, a Shido (minor penalty) does not end the match unless it is the athlete's third and final penalty.
Tactical Shift: Athletes often change their strategy in Golden Score, becoming either more aggressive to find a quick score or more defensive to avoid a tie-breaking penalty.
questions.conceptTested: Official International Judo Federation (IJF) regulations for overtime/Golden Score periods.

questions.testName: SSC CGL 2026 [Sectional Timing] - Tier I- 3
questions.question: In the context of the GST Council, what constitutes the 'quorum' for a meeting?
questions.solution:
The Quorum Rule: According to Article 279A of the Indian Constitution, the quorum for any meeting of the GST Council is one-half (50%) of its total members. This means at least 50% of the members (including the Union and State representatives) must be present for the Council to transact any business.
Definition of Quorum: Quorum refers to the minimum number of members of a deliberative body necessary to conduct the business of that group and make proceedings valid.

Further Insights:
Decision Making: While the quorum is 50%, the decisions of the GST Council are taken by a majority of not less than three-fourths (75%) of the weighted votes of the members present and voting.
Weightage of Votes: The Union Government has a weightage of one-third of the total votes cast, while all the State Governments combined have a weightage of two-thirds of the total votes cast in that meeting.
Council Composition: The Council is chaired by the Union Finance Minister and includes the Union Minister of State in charge of Revenue or Finance and the Ministers in charge of Finance or Taxation of all the States.

questions.question: The 'groundnut fair' known as Kadalekai Parishe in Bengaluru is associated historically with which temple/figure?

options.a: ISKCON Temple and offering of sugarcane
options.b: Vidhana Soudha and agricultural subsidies launch
options.c: Tipu Sultan’s memorial and incense offerings
options.d: Dodda Ganesha, Bull Temple or Nandi Basava

questions.solution:
Solution

The correct answer is Dodda Ganesha, Bull Temple or Nandi Basava.

Key Points
Kadalekai Parishe is a traditional groundnut fair held annually in Bengaluru, Karnataka, with deep religious and cultural significance.
The fair is historically associated with the Bull Temple (Dodda Basavana Gudi), which is dedicated to Nandi Basava, the sacred bull of Lord Shiva.
Devotees offer freshly harvested groundnuts (kadalekai) to Nandi as part of a traditional ritual seeking prosperity, good harvest, and agricultural well-being.
The nearby Dodda Ganesha Temple is also closely linked to the festivities, and offerings are made to Lord Ganesha before visiting the Bull Temple.
Hence, the association of Kadalekai Parishe is correctly linked with Dodda Ganesha, Bull Temple, and Nandi Basava, making option 4 the correct answer.

Additional Information
Location: The fair is held in the Basavanagudi area of Bengaluru, which is one of the city’s oldest residential and cultural localities.
Historical Origin: Kadalekai Parishe dates back over five centuries, originating during the reign of the Vijayanagara Empire, when farmers offered their produce to temples after harvest.
Religious Significance: Nandi Basava is regarded as the guardian deity of agriculture and fertility, making the offering of groundnuts symbolically important for farming communities.
Timing: The fair is usually conducted during the Kartika month (October-November), coinciding with the groundnut harvest season in southern India.
Incorrect Options Explained:
ISKCON Temple is associated with Vaishnavite worship and not with Kadalekai Parishe.
Vidhana Soudha is a legislative building and has no religious or agricultural fair association.
Tipu Sultan’s memorial is unrelated to groundnut offerings or this traditional festival.

questions.question: Which pair of Kashmiri musical form and its description is correctly matched?

options.a: Chakri - A classical genre performed with Santoor and Hafiz Nagma
options.b: Sufiana - A folk tradition sung using Garaha and Rabab
options.c: Hafiz Nagma - A dance form derived from Sufiana musical notes
options.d: Rouf - Instrumental duet using Santoor and Sitar

questions.solution:
Solution

The correct answer is Hafiz Nagma - A dance form derived from Sufiana musical notes.

Key Points
Hafiz Nagma:
Hafiz Nagma is a traditional dance form of Kashmir that is closely associated with Sufiana music.
It is performed by a female dancer, often referred to as the Hafiza, who interprets the Sufiana Kalam (mystical poetry) through her dance movements.
The music accompaniment for Hafiz Nagma consists of instruments like the Santoor, Sitar, and Tabla.
The dance movements are derived from the musical notes of Sufiana music, making it a unique blend of visual and auditory art. Hence, this statement is correct.
Chakri:
Chakri is a traditional folk music form of Kashmir. It is not a classical genre, and its primary instruments include the Harmonium and Rabab, not the Santoor.
Chakri is used to narrate folk tales or devotional themes in a simple yet captivating manner.
It is often performed during weddings and social gatherings to entertain the audience. Hence, this statement is incorrect.
Sufiana:
Sufiana music is a classical music tradition of Kashmir that is deeply rooted in Persian and Central Asian influences.
It is performed using traditional instruments like the Santoor, Kashmiri Saz, and Tabla, not Garaha and Rabab as mentioned in the question.
Sufiana music often serves as a medium for expressing mystical and spiritual themes. Hence, this statement is incorrect.
Rouf:
Rouf is a traditional dance form of Kashmiri women, typically performed during festivals like Eid or during weddings.
It involves rhythmic clapping and synchronized foot movements, accompanied by simple songs.
Rouf is not an instrumental duet involving Santoor and Sitar, as mentioned in the question. Hence, this statement is incorrect.

Additional Information
Importance of Kashmiri Music and Dance Forms:
Kashmiri music and dance forms are a reflection of the region's rich cultural heritage and traditions.
They often incorporate themes of nature, spirituality, and folklore, providing insight into the lives of Kashmiri people.
These art forms are performed during festivals, weddings, and other social gatherings, serving as a medium of entertainment and expression.
Specific Characteristics of Kashmiri Musical Forms:
Chakri: Known for its simple and repetitive musical patterns, Chakri often features themes of love, devotion, and folklore.
Sufiana: This music form is influenced by Persian classical music and focuses on mystical and spiritual themes, often using Persian poetry as its base.
Hafiz Nagma: This is a rare combination of music and dance, showcasing the artistic synergy between visual and auditory expressions.
Rouf: A vibrant dance form that emphasizes community bonding and celebration through synchronized movements and clapping.
Instruments Used in Kashmiri Music:
Santoor: A string instrument played by striking the strings with mallets.
Rabab: A lute-like instrument often used in folk and classical music.
Tabla: A percussion instrument that provides rhythmic accompaniment.
Sitar: A plucked string instrument used in both Indian and Kashmiri classical music.

Important Points

Preservation of Kashmiri Traditions:
Efforts are being made to preserve the unique art forms of Kashmir through cultural programs and festivals.
Organizations and artists are working towards documenting and promoting these traditions globally.
Role of Sufi Influence:
The Sufi tradition has had a profound impact on Kashmiri music, emphasizing mysticism and spirituality.
Many Kashmiri art forms, including Hafiz Nagma and Sufiana, are rooted in the Sufi philosophy of love and devotion.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): The policy of paramountcy allowed the British to interfere in Indian princely states' administration.
Reason
(R): Paramountcy meant that the British had the final authority in all military and foreign affairs.

options.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.c: A is true, but R is false.
options.d: A is false, but R is true.

questions.solution:
Solution

The correct answer is - Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.

Key Points
Policy of Paramountcy
The policy of paramountcy was a doctrine introduced by the British East India Company.
It allowed the British to assert their authority over Indian princely states.
Under this policy, the British could interfere in the administration of these states.
This policy was a significant tool for the British to maintain control over India's fragmented political landscape.
Military and Foreign Affairs
Paramountcy meant that the British had the final authority in all military and foreign affairs of the princely states.
This ensured that the princely states could not form alliances or engage in military actions without British approval.
It reinforced British dominance and prevented any potential unified resistance against British rule.

Additional Information
Doctrine of Lapse
A related policy was the Doctrine of Lapse, which allowed the British to annex princely states if the ruler died without a male heir.
This doctrine was also used to expand British territories in India.
Subsidiary Alliance
The Subsidiary Alliance was another strategy used by the British to control Indian states.
Under this system, Indian rulers were required to keep British forces in their territory and pay for their maintenance.
This further solidified British control over the Indian subcontinent.
British Residency System
British Residents were officials appointed to Indian princely states to oversee their administration.
They acted as intermediaries between the British government and the princely states.
This system ensured that the princely states remained under close British supervision.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the physiographic divisions of the Northern Plains of India:

i. The Terai region is a narrow belt along the foothills of the Shiwaliks composed of coarse pebbles where rivers disappear underground.

ii. The Bhabar region lies south of the foothills where underground streams re-emerge, creating a wet, marshy, and heavily forested zone.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
Both statements are incorrect.

The features of the Bhabar and Terai regions have been interchanged.

The Bhabar is the narrow belt of coarse pebbles along the foothills of the Shiwaliks where rivers disappear underground.

South of the Bhabar lies the Terai, where these underground streams re - emerge, creating a wet, marshy and formerly densely forested region.

Bhabar → Pebbles + Rivers disappear.

Terai → Rivers re - emerge + Marshy land.

Further Insights: • The Bhabar belt is approximately 8 - 16 km wide and lies parallel to the Shiwalik foothills.
• The Terai was once a densely forested region rich in wildlife; much of it has since been cleared for agriculture and settlement.
• Dudhwa National Park in Uttar Pradesh is located in the Terai region and is an important protected area of the Northern Plains.
• The Bhabar belt consists of boulders, pebbles and coarse sediments, making it highly porous and causing streams to disappear underground.

questions.question: Which of the following weather monitoring systems was inaugurated by IITM Pune at Mahabaleshwar under Mission Mausam, aimed at improving short-term forecasting and real-time atmospheric tracking across Maharashtra regions in April 2026?
questions.solution:
In Maharashtra, the Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology (IITM) in Pune, recently commissioned a new X - band Doppler Weather Radar at Mahabaleshwar under Mission Mausam.

The radar was inaugurated by M. Ravichandran in the presence of senior scientists and officials from IITM and ISRO on 24th of this month.

Installed at an altitude of around 1, 400 metres in the Western Ghats, the radar acts as a weather eye in the sky, continuously monitoring atmospheric conditions.

It can track rainfall, clouds, storms, fog and strong winds in real time, and is expected to improve short - term weather forecasts of up to three hours for regions including Satara, Pune, Konkan and Mumbai. On the occasion, IITM also signed an MoU with ISRO\'s Space Applications Centre (SAC) to jointly develop improved satellite - based weather products aimed at strengthening forecasts related to climate change, lightning, deep convection and air quality.

The system is expected to support flood and landslide warnings, aviation safety, agriculture advisory, disaster management and water resource planning.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: The devotional composition "Guru Bin Kaun Bataaye" is commonly rendered in the tala known as ____
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Teentaal.

Key Points
The devotional composition "Guru Bin Kaun Bataaye" is commonly rendered in the tala known as Teentaal. It is one of the most widely used and versatile talas in Hindustani classical music.

Teentaal consists of 16 beats, divided into four equal sections (vibhags) of four beats each.

This tala is known for its balanced structure, making it suitable for both vocal and instrumental performances, as well as for compositions such as devotional songs.

The first beat of Teentaal is called Sam, and it marks the most emphasized point in the tala cycle, serving as a reference for rhythm.

questions.testName: SSC CGL 2026 Free Live mock 42 (MEP-7)
questions.question: For a concave mirror, an object is placed at $u = -15\text{ cm}$ and the focal length is $f = -10\text{ cm}$. Find the image distance $v$.
questions.solution:
Answer: Option (a) - -30 cm

By the mirror formula $\frac{1}{v} + \frac{1}{u} = \frac{1}{f}$, we get $\frac{1}{v} = \frac{1}{f} - \frac{1}{u} = -\frac{1}{10} + \frac{1}{15} = -\frac{1}{30}$, so $v = -30\text{ cm}$ - a real, inverted, enlarged image 30 cm in front of the mirror.

Revision note - mirror formula and magnification

The mirror formula is $\frac{1}{v} + \frac{1}{u} = \frac{1}{f}$, and the radius of curvature $R = 2f$.

Under the Cartesian sign convention distances are measured from the pole, with the incident ray direction taken as positive.

For a concave mirror $f$ is negative; for a convex mirror $f$ is positive.

Magnification $m = -\frac{v}{u} = \frac{h'}{h}$. A negative $m$ means a real, inverted image; a positive $m$ means a virtual, erect image.

questions.solution:
Answer: Option (d) - The left ventricle pumps oxygenated blood to the whole body.

The left ventricle receives oxygenated blood from the left atrium and pumps it into the aorta for the whole body. Its wall is the thickest of the four chambers.

Revision note - the human heart and double circulation

The human heart has four chambers: two atria above and two ventricles below.

Deoxygenated blood from the body reaches the right atrium through the superior and inferior vena cava.

From the right ventricle it goes to the lungs through the pulmonary artery - the only artery carrying deoxygenated blood.

questions.solution:
Statement I is incorrect. The Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) is a survey - based indicator, compiled from responses of purchasing managers regarding variables such as new orders, output/business activity, employment, suppliers’ delivery times and inventories. questions.question: Which of the following best describes the contribution of Tyagaraja to Indian classical music?

options.a: He codified Hindustani ragas into a ten-parent-scale (that) system and authored music treatises in Sanskrit.
options.b: He composed thousands of devotional kritis in Telugu and Sanskrit addressed to Lord Rama, and is regarded as one of the three pillars of Carnatic music.
options.c: He invented the sitar and introduced Persian melodic concepts into the Hindustani tradition during the Mughal period.
options.d: He pioneered the Khyal form of singing as a successor to Dhrupad, composing bandishes in Braj Bhasha.

questions.solution:
Tyagaraja (1767 - 1847) is a towering figure in the history of Carnatic music (the classical music of South India). His contributions are central to the art form as we know it today.

Key Contributions of Tyagaraja: - The Trinity of Carnatic Music: Along with Muthuswami Dikshitar and Syama Sastri, Tyagaraja is one of the "Trinity" (Trimurti) who shaped the modern Carnatic tradition. - The Kriti Format: He perfected the kriti (a devotional song format), focusing on the structure of Pallavi, Anupallavi, and Charanam. - Devotion to Rama: Most of his compositions are deeply spiritual and dedicated to Lord Rama. His works, such as the Pancharatna Kritis (Five Gems), are celebrated for their poetic beauty and technical complexity. - Innovations in Raga: He is credited with introducing many new ragas and popularizing the use of Sangatis - variations on a melodic line that gradually reveal the depth of a raga.
Why the other options are incorrect: - A: This describes Vishnu Narayan Bhatkhande, who codified the Thaat system in Hindustani music. - C: This is traditionally attributed to Amir Khusrau, a Sufi musician and poet of the 13th century. - D: This refers to the evolution of Hindustani music styles, often associated with figures like Niyamat Khan (Sadarang).
questions.conceptTested: Historical personalities and major milestones in the evolution of Carnatic and Hindustani classical music traditions.

tags.conceptTested: Historical personalities and major milestones in the evolution of Carnatic and Hindustani classical music traditions.

questions.testName: SSC CGL 2026 [Sectional Timing] - Tier I 2026 Live Test
questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the characteristics and crop suitability of Indian soils:
Statement I: Black soils exhibit a high moisture-retaining capacity due to their clayey composition, causing them to swell when wet and develop deep cracks when dry.
Statement II: Black soils are rich in lime, iron, magnesia and alumina, but are generally deficient in phosphoric acid, nitrogen and organic matter.
Statement III: Owing to their physical and chemical characteristics, black soils are suitable for the cultivation of crops such as cotton, sugarcane, jowar and wheat.
Statement IV: Tea plants thrive exceptionally well in deep, waterlogged clay basins of black soil regions, whereas apple orchards grow best in the acidic loamy variations of laterite soils.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

options.a:
Only
Statement II,
Statement III and
Statement IV
options.b:
Only
Statement I,
Statement III and
Statement IV
options.c:
Only
Statement I,
Statement II and
Statement III
options.d:
Statement I,
Statement II,
Statement III and
Statement IV

questions.solution:
Statement I is correct

Black soils are generally clayey and possess a high capacity to retain moisture.

During the wet season, these soils absorb water and swell, whereas in the dry season they shrink and develop wide and deep cracks.

Statement II is correct

Black soils contain important mineral constituents such as lime, iron, magnesia and alumina.

However, they are generally deficient in phosphoric acid, nitrogen and organic matter.

Statement III is correct

The moisture - retaining and nutrient characteristics of black soils make them suitable for several crops.

Cotton is particularly associated with black soil, while crops such as sugarcane, jowar and wheat are also cultivated in these soils.

Statement IV is incorrect

Tea requires well - drained soil and does not thrive in waterlogged black clay basins.

Apple cultivation is mainly associated with suitable temperate climatic conditions and well - drained soils rather than laterite soils as a general rule.
questions.conceptTested: Characteristics, mineral composition, and crop suitability of Indian soils such as black soil.

tags.conceptTested: Characteristics, mineral composition, and crop suitability of Indian soils such as black soil.

The Correct answer is Chad.

Key Points
The Nile River is the longest river in the world, stretching approximately 6, 650 kilometers (4, 130 miles).

It flows through 11 countries, including Egypt, Sudan, South Sudan, Uganda, and Ethiopia, among others.

The river is divided into two major tributaries: the White Nile, which originates in Lake Victoria (Uganda), and the Blue Nile, which originates in Lake Tana (Ethiopia).

The Nile plays a crucial role in supporting agriculture, as its waters are used for irrigation in arid regions, especially in Egypt and Sudan.

Chad, however, is not located along the Nile River or its tributaries. It lies to the west of Sudan and is part of the Lake Chad Basin, which is a different hydrological system.

Statement I: A piece of iron placed in a solution of copper sulfate gradually develops a reddish layer.
Statement II: Copper is more reactive than iron and replaces it in the solution.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Only Statement 1 is true.

Statement I is correct because iron is more reactive than copper. When placed in a copper sulfate solution, iron displaces copper and forms iron sulfate while copper gets deposited on the iron surface as a reddish layer ($Fe + CuSO_4 \to FeSO_4 + Cu$).
Statement II is incorrect because copper is less reactive than iron and cannot replace iron from its salt solution.

questions.testName: SSC CGL 2026: Officer’s Friday - Mega Live Test
questions.question: Vice President C P Radhakrishnan inaugurated the 39th Surajkund International Crafts Mela at Surajkund in Faridabad, Haryana. What is the theme of this mela?

options.b: Artisans of India: Past and Present

questions.solution:
Solution

The correct answer is Local to Global - Atmanirbhar Bharat.

Key Points
The 39th Surajkund International Crafts Mela 2026 (from 31 January to 15 February 2026) was inaugurated by Vice President C P Radhakrishnan at Surajkund in Faridabad, Haryana. This annual event is recognized as the world's largest crafts fair, showcasing the rich diversity of traditional Indian handicrafts.
The theme for the 2026 mela is Local to Global - Atmanirbhar Bharat. This theme aligns with the Government of India's mission to promote indigenous products on an international stage and foster a self-reliant economy through the Make in India and Vocal for Local initiatives.
The mela provides a massive platform for artisans, weavers, and sculptors from across India and over 20 participating countries to demonstrate their traditional skills and sell their products directly to consumers.
Uttar Pradesh and Meghalaya were chosen as the theme states for the 2026.
Egypt participated as the partner nation of the fair for the year 2026.
The event is organized by the Surajkund Mela Authority and Haryana Tourism in collaboration with the Union Ministries of Tourism, Textiles, Culture, and External Affairs. It typically takes place in the month of February every year.
The 39th edition emphasizes the fusion of traditional heritage with modern marketing, helping local handicraft industries reach global markets, thereby enhancing the socio-economic status of rural artisans.

Additional Information
History and Significance: The Surajkund Crafts Mela was first hosted in 1987 to provide a platform for skilled artisans who were facing challenges from machine-made goods. Over the decades, it has grown from a national fair to an international cultural phenomenon.
Location Heritage: The mela is held near the Surajkund reservoir, an ancient 10th-century water tank built by King Suraj Pal of the Tomar dynasty. The site offers a historical backdrop that complements the traditional theme of the fair.
Theme State and Partner Nation: Each year, the mela features a specific Theme State and a Partner Nation. The Theme State showcases its unique architecture, folk arts, and culinary traditions through a specially designed permanent gate and complex within the mela grounds.

questions.testName: SSC CGL 2026: Officer’s Friday - Mega Live Test
questions.question: According to the nebular hypothesis, what did the solar system form from?

options.c: A rotating cloud of gas and dust

questions.solution:
Solution

The correct answer is 'A rotating cloud of gas and dust.'

Key Points
Nebular Hypothesis:
The nebular hypothesis suggests that the Solar System formed about 4.6 billion years ago from a large, rotating cloud of interstellar gas and dust, known as the solar nebula.
This cloud began to collapse under its own gravity, leading to the formation of a protostar (the Sun) at the center of the nebula.
As the cloud continued to collapse, it began to spin faster and flatten into a disk shape due to the conservation of angular momentum.
Within this rotating disk, particles of dust and ice collided and stuck together, gradually forming planets, moons, asteroids, and other small Solar System bodies through a process called accretion.

Additional Information
Exploding Star:
While a nearby supernova (exploding star) may have triggered the collapse of the solar nebula, the Solar System itself did not form directly from an exploding star.
Supernovae can contribute to the material in a nebula by enriching it with heavy elements, but the Solar System formation process follows from the collapse and evolution of the solar nebula.
Giant Asteroid:
The Solar System did not form from a giant asteroid. Asteroids are remnants of the material from the early Solar System that never coalesced into a planet.
Colliding Comets:
The colliding comets theory is not a part of the nebular hypothesis. Comets are small icy bodies that formed from the outer regions of the solar nebula.

Important Points

The nebular hypothesis is the most widely accepted model for the formation of the Solar System.
It accounts for many observed features of the Solar System, such as the predominantly flat, disk-like structure and the orderly orbits of the planets around the Sun.
The process of accretion within the nebular disk explains the formation of diverse bodies, from large planets to small asteroids and comets.
Understanding the nebular hypothesis provides insights into the formation of other planetary systems throughout the universe.

questions.question: Who is the author of "India’s First Radicals: Young Bengal and the British Empire"?

In News
‘India’s First Radicals’ by Rosinka Chaudhuri.

Key Points
Henry Derozio, a 17-year-old Anglo-Portuguese poet, became a lecturer at Hindu College, Calcutta in 1826.

Dismissed in 1831 for propagating atheism, Derozio died shortly after, but his students continued his legacy.

His poetry, especially The Fakeer of Jungheera, expressed nationalist anguish and a call for freedom.

Derozio inspired the Academic Association, promoting liberty, reason, and reformist debate.

The Derozians evolved into Young Bengal, a radical group challenging religious and social orthodoxy.

In 1843, they founded Bengal British India Society, India’s first political party, aiming for egalitarian ideals.

Their vision contrasted with Macaulay's anglicized elite, and they were called “a new race of men in the East” by Alexander Duff.

Young Bengal’s ideals of inclusivity, tolerance, and intellectual openness prefigured the visions of Gandhi and Nehru.

Eminent writer and literature stalwart Rosinka Chaudhuri’s “India’s First Radicals: Young Bengal and the British Empire“, delves into the transformative intellectual movement of the Young Bengal group, a collective of early 19th-century reformers led by Henry Derozio.

Solution

Key Points
Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD)
ASD is a complex developmental condition that involves persistent challenges in social interaction, speech and nonverbal communication, and restricted/repetitive behaviors.
The term spectrum is used because the symptoms and their severity vary significantly from one person to another.
It is typically diagnosed in early childhood, often by age 2 or 3, as developmental delays become more apparent.

Additional Information
Characteristics of ASD
Social Communication: Difficulty in understanding social cues, maintaining conversations, or expressing emotions.
Repetitive Behaviors: Engaging in repetitive body movements (e.g., hand flapping), insistence on sameness or routines, and intense interests in specific topics.
Sensory Sensitivity: Over-sensitivity or under-sensitivity to sensory stimuli like light, sound, or touch.
Global Awareness
World Autism Awareness Day is observed every year on April 2nd to increase understanding and acceptance of people with autism.
Early intervention through behavioral therapies and educational support can significantly improve the quality of life for individuals with ASD.

questions.question: For an object moving with uniform speed, what does the distance-time graph for such motion look like?

options.a: A curved line showing changing slope
options.b: A straight line inclined to the time axis
options.d: A straight line parallel to the time axis

questions.solution:
Solution
The correct answer is A straight line inclined to the time axis.

Key Points
Uniform speed is defined as a type of motion where an object covers equal distances in equal intervals of time.
In a distance-time graph, the distance is plotted on the Y-axis and the time is plotted on the X-axis.
The slope of a distance-time graph represents the speed of the object.
Since the speed is constant (uniform), the slope of the graph must also be constant.
A graph with a constant slope is represented by a straight line.
For uniform speed, this straight line must be inclined to the time axis, indicating that distance increases steadily as time progresses.

Additional Information
If the distance-time graph is a straight line parallel to the time axis, the speed is zero (the object is at rest).
If the graph is a curved line, it represents non-uniform motion, where the speed is changing over time.
The steeper the slope of the straight line, the higher the uniform speed of the object.
Mathematical relation: Speed = Distance / Time. In a linear graph, this is expressed as y = mx, where m is the constant speed.
