questions.question: According to the Economic Survey, fiscal consolidation primarily aims to:

options.b: Create fiscal space while supporting growth
options.c: Eliminate revenue deficit in the short term
options.d: Replace revenue expenditure with capital expenditure entirely

questions.solution:
Solution
The correct answer is Option B.

Key Points
The Economic Survey clarifies that fiscal consolidation is not synonymous with fiscal contraction.
Its primary objective is to create fiscal space so that the government can respond to shocks, fund priority spending, and maintain macro-economic stability, while still supporting economic growth.
Consolidation focuses on improving the quality of expenditure (especially higher capital expenditure), enhancing revenue efficiency, and maintaining credibility.
It does not imply:
indiscriminate cuts in welfare spending,
immediate elimination of revenue deficit regardless of growth conditions, or
complete replacement of revenue expenditure with capital expenditure.

Thus, fiscal consolidation aims to create fiscal space while supporting growth → Option B.

Additional Information
The Survey stresses growth-friendly fiscal consolidation, where public capex acts as a multiplier for private investment.
Maintaining fiscal credibility helps reduce borrowing costs and strengthens investor confidence.
Medium-term consolidation is preferred over abrupt fiscal tightening to avoid derailing recovery.

questions.question: Which of the following statements correctly describes Newton\'s Second Law of Motion?

options.a: Every object continues in its state of rest or uniform motion in a straight line unless acted upon by an external unbalanced force.
options.b: The rate of change of momentum of an object is directly proportional to the applied unbalanced force and takes place in the direction of the force.
options.c: To every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction that acts simultaneously on the same body to maintain equilibrium.
options.d: The net electrostatic force between two point charges is inversely proportional to the product of their masses and distance squared.

questions.solution:
Newton\'s Second Law of Motion states that the rate of change of momentum of an object is directly proportional to the applied unbalanced force and occurs in the direction of the force. Mathematically, for a constant mass, this gives the relation $F = ma$.

Option (a): This statement describes Newton\'s First Law of Motion, also known as the Law of Inertia.
Option (c): This statement refers to Newton\'s Third Law of Motion. Moreover, action and reaction act on two different bodies, not on the same body.
Option (d): This statement is unrelated to Newton\'s Laws of Motion. It incorrectly mixes electrostatic force with mass.
Further Insights: • Momentum is the product of mass and velocity: $p = mv$.
• The SI unit of force is the newton (N), where $1\text{ N} = 1\text{ kg m s}^{-2}$.
• A force of one newton produces an acceleration of $1\text{ m/s}^2$ in a body of mass $1\text{ kg}$.

Key Points: - The Goods and Services Tax (GST) was introduced in India through the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016, following the passage of the 122nd Constitution Amendment Bill in Parliament. - It is a comprehensive, multi - stage, destination - based tax that replaced various indirect taxes such as Excise Duty, VAT, Service Tax, and Luxury Tax to create a unified national market. - The amendment inserted Article 246A into the Constitution, granting both the Union and State legislatures the power to make laws with respect to GST. - It also established the GST Council under Article 279A, chaired by the Union Finance Minister, to make recommendations on tax rates, exemptions, and administrative thresholds. - The GST regime officially came into effect across India on July 1, 2017.

Key Points: - The Bering Strait is a vital geographical waterway that separates the continents of North America and Asia at their closest point. - Geographically, it is situated between Cape Dezhnev, the easternmost point of the Chukchi Peninsula in Russia, and Cape Prince of Wales, the westernmost point of the Seward Peninsula in Alaska, United States. - The strait measures approximately 82 kilometers (51 miles) in width at its narrowest point and has a relatively shallow depth, ranging between 30 to 50 meters. - It serves as the critical marine gateway connecting the Chukchi Sea (part of the Arctic Ocean) to the north with the Bering Sea (part of the Pacific Ocean) to the south. - The International Date Line runs between the Diomede Islands (Big Diomede in Russia and Little Diomede in the USA) located in the middle of the strait, meaning the two islands are in different calendar days despite being only 3.8 kilometers apart.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Full Test - 24
questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding ozone depletion:
I. One chlorine atom can destroy only a few ozone molecules before it is removed from the stratosphere.
II. All chlorine and bromine sources contribute equally to ozone layer depletion.
Which of the above statements is/are incorrect?
questions.solution:
Statement I: A single chlorine atom participates in a catalytic cycle, destroying thousands of ozone molecules before being removed from the reactive cycle. Hence, Statement I is incorrect.
Statement II: All chlorine - and bromine - containing substances do not contribute equally to ozone depletion. Their impact depends on factors such as atmospheric lifetime, ability to reach the stratosphere, and ozone - depletion potential (ODP). Hence, Statement II is incorrect.
Therefore, both Statements I and II are incorrect.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding Non-Performing Assets (NPAs):
I. A loan is generally classified as NPA if interest or principal remains overdue for more than 90 days.
II. Higher NPAs reduce the profitability and lending capacity of banks.
III. Priority Sector Lending is the sole reason behind rising NPAs in India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is I and II only.

Key Points: - Statement I: As a general prudential norm, a loan is classified as an NPA when interest and/or principal remains overdue for more than 90 days. Hence, Statement I is correct. - Statement II: Higher NPAs reduce banks’ interest income, increase provisioning requirements, weaken profitability and constrain their ability to extend fresh credit. Hence, Statement II is correct. - Statement III: Priority Sector Lending is not the sole reason for rising NPAs. NPAs may arise due to poor credit appraisal, economic slowdown, project delays, sectoral stress, and other factors. Hence, Statement III is incorrect.

questions.testName: SSC CGL 2026 [Sectional Timing] - Tier I 2026 Live Test
questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding categories of goods in an economy:
Statement I: Intermediate goods are final goods that pass out of the active economic flow and undergo no further transformation by producers.
Statement II: Capital goods are completely consumed or transformed within a single cycle of the production process like raw materials.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.c:
Both
Statement I and
Statement II
options.d:
Neither
Statement I nor
Statement II

questions.solution:
Statement I is incorrect.

The description given actually refers to final goods, not intermediate goods.

Intermediate goods are goods used as inputs in the production of other goods and are transformed during the production process.

Final goods pass out of the active economic flow after being sold and undergo no further transformation by producers.

Statement II is incorrect.

Capital goods are durable producer goods such as machines, equipment, and factory buildings that are used repeatedly in the production process over several years.

They are not completely consumed or transformed in a single production cycle like raw materials or intermediate goods.
questions.conceptTested: Definitions and distinctions between intermediate goods, final goods, and capital goods in economic circular flow.

questions.question: Which chemical is used for artificial rain?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Silver Iodide.

Artificial rain, also known as cloud seeding, is a process by which specific chemicals are introduced into clouds to stimulate precipitation. The most commonly used chemical for this process is Silver Iodide.

Silver Iodide serves as an effective nucleating agent because its crystalline structure is similar to that of ice. This similarity allows it to promote the formation of ice crystals in clouds, which grow and eventually fall as precipitation. Hence, Silver Iodide is widely used in artificial rain creation.

questions.question: The fiscal deficit target of the Union Government for Budget 2026-27 is approximately what percentage of GDP?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 4.3\%.

Key Points
The fiscal deficit represents the difference between the total revenue and total expenditure of the government, excluding borrowings. It is a crucial indicator of a country\'s financial health.

For the Union Budget 2026 - 27, the fiscal deficit target has been set at approximately 4.3\% of GDP, which aligns with the government\'s goal of fiscal consolidation.

The fiscal deficit reflects the government\'s borrowing requirements to bridge the gap between revenue and expenditure. A lower deficit is indicative of financial discipline and economic stability.

The government has been consistently working to reduce the fiscal deficit to ensure compliance with the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Act, which mandates prudent fiscal management.

By targeting a fiscal deficit of 4.3\%, the government aims to achieve a balance between economic growth and financial sustainability.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 14
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct about a Money Bill?

options.a: A money bill can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha on the recommendation of the Speaker of Lok Sabha.
options.b: The Rajya Sabha has the power to reject a money bill.
options.c: The Lok Sabha can either accept or reject all or any of the recommendations of the Rajya Sabha.
options.d: If there is a deadlock between the two Houses over the passage of a bill, the president can summon a joint sitting.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is The Lok Sabha can either accept or reject all or any of the recommendations of the Rajya Sabha.

Explanation: - A Money Bill can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha on the recommendation of the President, not the Speaker (Option A is incorrect). - The Rajya Sabha cannot reject or amend a Money Bill; it can only make recommendations within 14 days (Option B is incorrect). - The Lok Sabha may accept or reject any or all of the recommendations made by the Rajya Sabha (Option C is correct). - There is no provision for a joint sitting in the case of a Money Bill (Option D is incorrect).

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 16
questions.question: Which of the following School of Art has more Indian features as compared to the others and is influenced by Buddhism, Hinduism and Jainism?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Mathura.

Key Points
In Mathura school of art, the sculptures of the Mathura school were influenced by all three religions Buddhism, Hinduism, and Jainism.

Initial Development: Developed in and around Mathura.
Patronage: This school was patronized by Kushan rulers.
Major Centres: Mathura, Sonkh and Kankalitila.
Key Feature: Symbolism in the images was one of the key features of the Mathura school of art. Shiva was represented using linga and mukhalinga, the halo around the head of Buddha was decorated with geometrical patterns and Buddha is shown to be surrounded by two Bodhisattvas - Padmapani (holding a lotus) and Vajrapani (holding a thunderbolt).

Gandhara school and Amravati are mainly influenced by Buddhism.

Greek school of art is influenced by Hellenism.

Hence we conclude that the correct answer is Mathura.

questions.testName: SSC CGL Tier I: Full Test - 16
questions.question: After which five year plan, "the Rolling Plan" was implemented?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Fifth five year plan.

Key Points
Rolling Plan in India was started in 1978.

The rolling plan concept was coined by Gunnar Myrdal.

This plan was rejected again by the Indian National Congress government when it came to power in 1980 and a new sixth plan was made.

The main advantage of the rolling plans is that they are flexible.

The Rolling Plan is a plan in which every year the performance of the plan is assessed and a new plan is made next year based on this assessment.

Thus, both the allocation and targets are revised during this plan.

In India, the Janta Government terminated the fifth five - year plan in 1977 - 78 and launched its own sixth five - year plan for the period 1978 - 83 and called it a Rolling Plan.
